body:
# Raw friction log: bd-01M16Z1ASRG30187SFYJ68JV0F

Actor: codex-storymodel-research-spike

1. Read the owner directive before choosing a number. The deliverable says to start from raw WOG text, not `WarOfTheGhostsModel`, and to stop at the first real researcher wall. I initially wanted to copy the fixture alignment test because it already computes coverage; that would defeat the bead.

2. `git status` printed hundreds of untracked `.mote/ops` files from live coordination before any research work appeared. This is shared-checkout noise, not yet a library API wall, but a cold researcher would not know whether the checkout was safe to use.

3. The root README is honest immediately: complete automatic construction from raw text is programme work; current story fixtures are hand modeled; there is no unattended text-to-AMR parser, LLM acquisition adapter, HTTP/ONNX provider, or calibrated production default.

4. The admitted raw source is findable at `docs/design/war-of-the-ghosts-boas1901.txt`, with provenance and admission metadata in its header. The same text also exists as Scala source in `WarOfTheGhostsText.scala`. I hesitated over which was actually authoritative. I chose the admitted text file because the directive says raw text.

5. The recall side is not a raw transcript file. Ten “manual recall paraphrases” are embedded as Scala values in `WarOfTheGhostsExpectations.scala`, alongside intended target IDs and notes. I can extract a sentence as text, but doing so already means discovering and reading a fixture implementation.

6. The README gives a public raw-text entry point: `StorySource.fromText` then `SurfaceAnalyzer.analyze`. I am executing that exact path on the admitted WOG file before reading around the missing next step.

7. My first attempt used `sbt coreJVM/console` with redirected REPL input. Sbt exited 0, but JLine left the input at an unfinished paste prompt and executed none of it. The exit code looked green. I had to inspect the log to discover there was no `SPIKE_SOURCE` line. A researcher copying the README into the project console could mistake process success for program execution.

8. I cloned the current checkout into `/tmp` and added a scratch `runMain`. I also had to write a parser that skips the admission header: passing the admitted `.txt` file directly to `StorySource.fromText` would make provenance metadata part of the story. There is no admitted-story loader or machine-readable boundary between header and text.

9. The public source surface path executed successfully on the admitted text: 2,180 canonical characters, 2 paragraphs, 50 sentences, 517 tokens, checksum `36c52efe94a95da4b1b6ba1df479f53bf51a74b751acfa75d2d84dea5924d93e`. Log: `/tmp/storymodel4s-e2e-raw-surface.log`.

10. I chose the first precise manual recall sentence because I need one source-versus-recall question and it is the least ambiguous fixture statement: “One of the men with him got hit by an arrow and they lifted him into the boat.” The candidate research question is: how locally specific is the source mass assigned to this recall, and how much aligned mass supports that specificity? `RecallSignature.specificityMass: MassRatio` has the required value plus conditioning and total mass.

11. The public recall path also executes from text. `RecallSegmenter.segment` produced 2 idea units from the one sentence, not the one unit used by the fixture expectation: (a) predicate `get`, lemmas arrow/get/hit/man; (b) predicate `lift`, lemmas boat/lift. Log: `/tmp/storymodel4s-e2e-raw-recall.log`.

12. I then noticed `WarOfTheGhostsAlignmentSuite.segmentOne` manually merges those two units because the fixture expectation is stated per sentence. A researcher has no public policy telling them whether the scientific unit is the segmenter's two clauses or the fixture author's one statement. Merging changes the trajectory and therefore the signature. I did not merge.

13. The aligner cannot consume `StorySource` or `SurfaceAtlas`. Its public bridge is `StorySourceView.validated(model: StoryModel[Validated])` (or adjudicated). The raw source path therefore needs a validated `StoryModel` before candidate generation or inference can start.

14. `StoryModel.draft` does not construct that missing representation. It requires the caller to supply a complete `NarrativeGraph`, `NarrativeHierarchy`, and `DiscourseTrajectory` (plus optional claims/features). `StoryValidator.validate` checks a draft; it does not infer one.

15. I was tempted to pass `NarrativeGraph.empty`, `NarrativeHierarchy.empty`, and `DiscourseTrajectory.empty` because those constructors exist. That might satisfy types or yield a validation result, but it would answer a question about an empty hand-built source, not WOG. This is exactly the kind of heroic bypass the directive says not to use.

16. `acquire` looked like the missing bridge by name. Its README says it is only pure portable protocol and deterministic logic: no I/O, HTTP, model client, or provider. Repository search confirms `TaskPacket` has no production construction site outside its definition; `Resolver.resolve`, `BuildPlan.from`, and `PatchApplier.applyPatch` are exercised only in tests; no production function consumes raw text or proposals and returns a `NarrativeGraph` or `StoryModel`.

17. The only production ways I found to obtain a `StoryModel` are: hand every component to `StoryModel.draft`, or decode already-constructed model JSON through the codec. The only production `StorySourceView` use outside the bridge is `embed-bench`, and it loads `WarOfTheGhostsModel.model`. The fixture alignment test does the same.

18. FIRST GENUINE WALL. Raw source text and raw recall text both reach deterministic surface/recall structures. There is no executable source-text-to-narrative-model acquisition path, provider adapter, or even a composition function joining the pure acquire contracts to `StoryModel`. Without hand-authoring the source graph—the prohibited bypass—I cannot construct `StorySourceView`, generate source candidates, run `GraphHsmm`, or compute the support-bearing `specificityMass`. I am stopping here rather than loading `WarOfTheGhostsModel` and pretending the construction path worked.
19. Cost at the first-wall checkpoint: the spike session began at 2026-08-29T14:34:57Z and the wall was confirmed at 2026-08-29T14:42:18Z (7m21s). I made one failed REPL attempt, one clean standalone clone (105 MB after the runs), and two scratch `runMain` probes. There were zero remote-provider/API calls, zero external-network calls, zero shared-source edits, and zero path reservations. The failed REPL took about 20 seconds; the source probe took about 25 seconds wall time (11 seconds reported after build load); the recall probe took about 42 seconds wall time (21 seconds reported after build load). Both scoped probes still loaded the whole sbt build and local grakern/gale/graph4s definitions.

20. Final spike state: no support-bearing recall-vs-source number was produced. Raw story ingestion and raw recall segmentation were executable, but reaching `RecallSignature.specificityMass` requires a validated source model, and the repository has no production raw-text/proposal-to-`StoryModel` constructor. Substituting the hand-authored fixture or an empty graph would erase the exact path under test, so I stopped at the first genuine wall as directed.
